headline: CPI at 7:30 SK decides whether Monday's chip rebound holds
tldr: Chips had their best day in months on Monday (SOX about +6.9%, MU +6.25% to $733.15) and Asia followed, but Nasdaq 100 futures are −0.3% and MU has faded to about $726 ahead of an 8:30 ET CPI print that a Fed governor has tied to a possible 50bp December hike.

headline: Nvidia down 5% on Huang probe; MU flat ahead of CPI
tldr: Nvidia's board opened an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy and the stock is down about 5% pre-market, but the rest of the chip complex is shrugging it off (Taiex +4.9%, Nasdaq 100 futures +0.4%), MU is roughly flat at about $685, and Tuesday's CPI (with December hike odds near 80%) is the bigger event.

headline: Chips bounce about 5% pre-market after SOX's worst day since 2020
tldr: SOX fell 12.25% to 9,011 Thursday and MU fell 17.5% to $656.39, and Asia sold off again overnight, but US chips are bouncing pre-market: SMH and SOXX are up about 5%, MU is about $703–$710 (+7–8%), and Nasdaq 100 futures are up about 1.5% even after a hot jobs report (+165K) pushed yields higher.

headline: Chip selloff deepens; MU indicated about 5% lower, near 200-day average
tldr: Asian memory stocks crashed for a second day, Qualcomm's weak guidance and a Bloomberg report that Micron paused its new Taiwan plant add to the pressure, and with Nasdaq 100 futures down about 1% and SMH down 3.7% at about 9:10 ET, MU (about $755) and SOX (about 9,900 implied) are set to open at fresh lows while the Dow keeps rallying.

headline: Blue wave hits AI infrastructure; MU indicated about 2.5% lower
tldr: Democrats won both chambers, and a Texas governor who has promised a data-center moratorium won too. That pulled money out of the AI build-out trade overnight. Nasdaq futures faded to about flat by 8:45 ET while the Dow rallied, and MU slid from +1.4% early to about −2.6% ($832.78) by 8:30 ET, even though AMD, Arista and Super Micro all beat.

headline: MU up about 3% pre-market after Monday's 5.8% drop; AMD reports tonight
tldr: Monday's chip bounce failed, MU closed at $833.59 (−5.78%) and Seoul and Taipei each fell 3.6% overnight. MU is still indicated about 2–3% higher near $850–$860 on a flat-to-firm Nasdaq, but tonight's AMD, Arista and Super Micro results and the election make this open easy to fade, as Monday's was.

headline: MU indicated about 2% higher as chips bounce despite Kioxia
tldr: Futures are up after Friday's chip rout, helped by Korea's strong chip exports, SK Hynix's 3.8% gain and lower oil, so MU is set to open about 2–3% higher near $905, with Kioxia's flat NAND outlook as the main risk.

headline: Kioxia's weak outlook hits memory after Friday's chip sell-off
tldr: US markets are closed today (Sunday) and reopen Monday at 9:30 ET (8:30 SK). Futures are up modestly after Friday's sell-off in chips, SK Hynix has recovered in Seoul, and Kioxia's flat profit outlook is the main new risk for memory stocks.
